Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

split one’s sides laughing phrase

also die laughing, laugh one’s head off, in stitches

classical

Ter. Eun. 3.1.42: rīsū ēmorīrī (Lewis & Short)

rīsū ēmorī

ēmorior, ēmorī, ēmortuus sum, with the ablative rīsū

die laughing

Latin dies of laughter, as English does: rīsū is the ablative of cause. Terence has the old infinitive ēmorīrī.

Other words

  • īlia rīsū dissolvere — split one’s sides laughing

    īlia, īlium n. pl., the flanks, with dissolvō, dissolvere, dissolvī, dissolūtum · also used · modern · Traupman 108: īlia sua rīsū dissolvere

    Not found in Lewis & Short or the loci collections in this form; Traupman is the only evidence. Lewis & Short s.v. contendō cites īlia rīsū from Ovid (A. A. 3.285), the flanks strained with laughter.

See also laugh, burst out laughing.
